info.title: FreeHoroscopeAPI
info.description: Free public JSON APIs for horoscope readings, tarot cards, planetary positions, Panchang and Sun/Moon times. No API key or account is required. Public data routes support GET and OPTIONS with cross-origin access without credentials. Horoscope responses use a data wrapper; tarot responses use nhits and cards; calculation responses have no wrapper. This document covers the public data API, not account management. All references are included in this file. Commercial and non-commercial API use is allowed with attribution. Include a visible Powered by FreeHoroscopeAPI link to https://freehoroscopeapi.com in your application, website, or public documentation. Upstream requests have a total deadline of 10 seconds for horoscopes and 30 seconds for calculations, including the response body. Successful upstream data must match the response schema. Gateway errors include a stable code and a readable error message.

get.description: Returns the current daily reading for one zodiac sign inside a data object. The only supported query parameter is sign; there is no date or day selector. Upstream responses are checked for required fields, a non-empty reading, a valid calendar date (or YYYY-MM for monthly readings), and a sign and period that match the request. The date is the provider's reading label; this validation does not guarantee freshness. The total upstream deadline is 10 seconds. No include or timezone parameter is supported. The response contains no timezone field.

get.description: Returns calculated planetary positions, not written horoscope readings. No data wrapper. All 12 bodies are included. Coordinates are optional but must be supplied as a pair. Sidereal output uses an approximate Lahiri model, with mean Rahu and Ketu. No houses or Ascendant are returned. The complete upstream body is checked against the response schema before it is returned. The total upstream deadline is 30 seconds. The timezone is derived from the coordinates and returned in the response; a timezone query parameter cannot override it.

get.description: Requires lat and one of lng, lon or long. The date defaults to local today. The window runs from sunrise to the next sunrise, with a labeled civil-day fallback if sunrise is unavailable. The entire calculation window must fall within 1900-01-01T00:00:00Z inclusive to 2053-01-01T00:00:00Z exclusive. Returns astronomical limbs using an approximate Lahiri model; festival and regional observance rules are not included. No data wrapper. The complete upstream body is checked against the response schema before it is returned. The total upstream deadline is 30 seconds. The timezone is derived from the coordinates and returned in the response; a timezone query parameter cannot override it. This endpoint has no include or timeformat parameter. Window and transition timestamps always use ISO-8601 with local UTC offsets.

get.summary: Get Sun, Moon and Rahu Kaal times
get.description: Requires lat and one of lng, lon or long. Defaults to local today and 12-hour event strings. Set timeformat=24 for ISO-8601 event timestamps. With no date parameter, available today/tomorrow summaries are also included. Events can be null at polar locations, and Rahu Kaal can be absent. include=moon_details adds a separate local-noon calculation. No data wrapper. The complete upstream body is checked against the response schema before it is returned. The total upstream deadline is 30 seconds. The timezone is derived from the coordinates and returned in the response; a timezone query parameter cannot override it.

200.description: Local Sun and Moon events, with optional periods and summaries.

400.description: Invalid coordinate, date, datetime, include option or calculation range.

Sign.name: sign
Sign.description: Zodiac sign for the reading. Allowed values are listed below. Values are case-insensitive; for example, aries and Aries select the same sign. There is no default.

Datetime.name: datetime
Datetime.description: Defaults to the current instant. Supply ISO-8601 with seconds and Z or an explicit UTC offset. Supported UTC instants: 1900-01-01 inclusive to 2053-01-01 exclusive. Fractional seconds may have up to six digits. Date-only values, missing offsets, leap seconds and -00:00 are rejected. URL-encode a positive offset sign as %2B. Coordinates do not infer the input timezone.
Datetime.x-default-description: The current instant in UTC when the parameter is omitted.

Zodiac.name: zodiac
Zodiac.description: Sidereal uses an approximate Lahiri model. Tropical results omit nakshatra and pada and return a null ayanamsa.

x-enumDescriptions.sidereal: Approximate Lahiri zodiac; includes nakshatra and pada.
x-enumDescriptions.tropical: Tropical zodiac; omits nakshatra and pada and sets ayanamsa to null.

Latitude.name: lat
Latitude.description: Latitude in degrees. For planetary positions, omit both coordinates or supply latitude and one longitude. Required when include=observer.
Latitude.x-default-description: Omit both coordinates for geocentric positions without location metadata.

RequiredLatitude.name: lat
RequiredLatitude.description: Latitude in degrees. Also supply lng, lon or long.

Longitude.name: lng
Longitude.description: Longitude in degrees. Required with lat unless lon or long is supplied. The API checks lng first, then lon, then long. OpenAPI cannot express this dependency between query parameters.
Longitude.x-default-description: Use lon, then long, if lng is absent. A longitude is required whenever lat is supplied.

LongitudeAlias.name: lon
LongitudeAlias.description: Alternative to lng. Used only when lng is absent. Supply lat as well.
LongitudeAlias.x-default-description: No default. This is an alternative longitude parameter, not an additional coordinate.

LongAlias.name: long
LongAlias.description: Alternative to lng and lon. Used only when both are absent. Supply lat as well.
LongAlias.x-default-description: No default. This is an alternative longitude parameter, not an additional coordinate.

Observer.name: include
Observer.description: Add observer positions for the ten physical bodies: Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune and Pluto. Includes altitude_deg, azimuth_deg, distance_km and above_horizon. Rahu and Ketu are not physical bodies. Requires lat and one of lng, lon or long. The geocentric bodies object is unchanged. This endpoint accepts only observer. Omit include or send an empty value for the standard response. The parameter is a comma-separated list; whitespace and duplicate entries are ignored. Unknown values return HTTP 400.
Observer.x-default-description: No extra fields. Omit include or leave its value empty.

Date.name: date
Date.description: Local calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Omit the parameter or leave it empty to use today in the timezone derived from the coordinates. Panchang uses the date to select sunrise through the next sunrise. For Sun and Moon times, an explicit date omits the live today and tomorrow summaries.
Date.x-default-description: Today in the timezone derived from the coordinates.

TimeFormat.name: timeformat
TimeFormat.description: Event time display. Use 12 for YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss AM/PM ±HHMM (for example, 2026-10-01T06:30:00 AM +0530). Use 24 for ISO-8601 with the local UTC offset (for example, 2026-10-01T06:30:00+05:30). The short sunrise and sunset values in today/tomorrow use h:mm AM/PM or HH:mm. moon.details.evaluated_at always uses ISO-8601. Only the exact strings 12 and 24 are accepted.

x-enumDescriptions.12: 12-hour event times with AM/PM and UTC offset. API default.
x-enumDescriptions.24: ISO-8601 event timestamps with UTC offset. Playground preset.

MoonDetails.name: include
MoonDetails.description: Add moon.details with illumination_pct, phase_angle_deg, evaluated_at and status. The calculation uses local noon on the selected date, not the current time. evaluated_at is always ISO-8601, independent of timeformat. Outside the supported UTC interval from 1900-01-01 inclusive to 2053-01-01 exclusive, illumination_pct and phase_angle_deg are null and status is outside_supported_range. This endpoint accepts only moon_details. Omit include or send an empty value for the standard response. The parameter is a comma-separated list; whitespace and duplicate entries are ignored. Unknown values return HTTP 400.
MoonDetails.x-default-description: No extra fields. Omit include or leave its value empty.

CardCount.name: n
CardCount.description: Requested number of distinct cards, as a positive base-10 integer. Default: 1. The response count is capped at the pool size: 22 when minor is false, or 78 when minor is true. For example, n=100 returns the complete selected pool. Zero, negative values and non-numeric values return HTTP 400. There is no pagination.

IncludeMinor.name: minor
IncludeMinor.description: Choose the random draw pool. The exact lowercase value true includes all 78 cards. false or an omitted parameter uses the 22 major arcana cards. The current API also treats other strings, including True and 1, as false; use true or false for portable requests.

x-enumDescriptions.false: Draw from the 22 major arcana cards.
x-enumDescriptions.true: Draw from the full deck of 78 cards.

timezone.description: IANA timezone identifier derived from the coordinates, for example Asia/Kolkata, Europe/London or America/New_York. UTC is the fallback if no timezone is found. The value can be any timezone returned by the location database; it is not a fixed list. timezone is a response field, not a supported query parameter. Local dates and event offsets follow this timezone, including daylight saving time where applicable. Present only when coordinates are supplied; it does not change the UTC datetime or geocentric positions.

status.description: normal for a day with crossings, polar_day for continuous daylight, polar_night for continuous darkness, or unavailable when the duration cannot be calculated.

cards.name: The Magician
cards.meaning_up: Skill, diplomacy, address, subtlety; sickness, pain, loss, disaster, snares of enemies; self-confidence, will; the Querent, if male.
cards.meaning_rev: Physician, Magus, mental disease, disgrace, disquiet.
cards.desc: A youthful figure in the robe of a magician, having the countenance of divine Apollo, with smile of confidence and shining eyes. Above his head is the mysterious sign of the Holy Spirit, the sign of life, like an endless cord, forming the figure 8 in a horizontal position . About his waist is a serpent-cincture, the serpent appearing to devour its own tail. This is familiar to most as a conventional symbol of eternity, but here it indicates more especially the eternity of attainment in the spirit. In the Magician's right hand is a wand raised towards heaven, while the left hand is pointing to the earth. This dual sign is known in very high grades of the Instituted Mysteries; it shews the descent of grace, virtue and light, drawn from things above and derived to things below. The suggestion throughout is therefore the possession and communication of the Powers and Gifts of the Spirit. On the table in front of the Magician are the symbols of the four Tarot suits, signifying the elements of natural life, which lie like counters before the adept, and he adapts them as he wills. Beneath are roses and lilies, the flos campi and lilium convallium, changed into garden flowers, to shew the culture of aspiration. This card signifies the divine motive in man, reflecting God, the will in the liberation of its union with that which is above. It is also the unity of individual being on all planes, and in a very high sense it is thought, in the fixation thereof. With further reference to what I have called the sign of life and its connexion with the number 8, it may be remembered that Christian Gnosticism speaks of rebirth in Christ as a change "unto the Ogdoad." The mystic number is termed Jerusalem above, the Land flowing with Milk and Honey, the Holy Spirit and the Land of the Lord. According to Martinism, 8 is the number of Christ.
